newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco El Teniente sees technology sales rising.
newsitem.headline: Codelco El Teniente sees technology sales rising.

text.p: El Teniente division of Chile's state-owned copper company Codelco is in talks for contracts to sell $200 million worth of technology to foreign firms, said general manager Fernando Riveri.
"We have offers underway from the United States, Iran, China, Peru and South Africa," Riveri told Reuters in an interview at the mine's headquarters.
The division recently signed a $55 million deal with Thai Copper Industries to install an El Teniente-type converter in its smelter.
The converter, designed by the division, is is an alternative to the Outokumpu -developed flash furnace technology.
The mine, Codelco's second largest division, has also signed a $15 million deal to build a converter at the Mexican copper smelter La Caridad, he said.
The mine is hoping to wrap up larger contracts in the near future, said Riveri.
"We are working with other options which are for $200 million...We hope that between South Africa and Iran we can tie up a deal of that amount," he said.
